title: Interteam dependency orchestration and SLA framework for roadmap continuity
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Goal: create an operational framework that orchestrates cross-team dependencies (Eng, Design, Security, Infra) so roadmap commitments have clear SLAs, handoff contracts, and automated visibility. Outcome: a lightweight dependency orchestration layer + SLA tiers + escalation flows + a Console dashboard widget that surfaces risk to PM/Eng leads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dependency registry UI populated for top 30 active initiatives with owner, ETA, severity, and blocking flag. 2) SLA tiers documented and agreed by Eng and Infra (SLA Tier 1: 2 business days for triage, Tier 2: 7 calendar days). 3) Escalation playbook with contact matrix and oncall steps tested in one live cross-team rollout. 4) Console dashboard shows real-time status for these dependencies and links back to Linear issues.
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with Eng/Design/Security/Infra leads. Agreed top 30 initiatives scope and initial risk scoring rubric.
2025-02-28: Draft SLA tiers circulated. Security requested explicit review windows for design artifacts (48 hours) and a formal threat model step for any infra-facing change.
2025-03-05: Prototype dependency CSV schema created and validated against three active projects (runtime-1.18 rollout, console-2025.02, private-deployments-onprem).
2025-03-10: Design mockups for dependency panel in Console v1 reviewed; design feedback: require owner avatars and one-click link to PR/Confluence.
2025-03-12: Engineering proposed a webhook sync approach from Linear -> Console and a minimal API for programmatic updates. Agreed to run a test with ENG-22134 and PM-13321.
decisions: Use a lightweight registry (CSV backlog -> Linear canonical source) rather than building a full separate service for MVP to reduce iteration cost.
Adopt three SLA tiers (P0/P1/P2) mapped to triage and resolution windows rather than a score continuum to simplify oncall routing.
Visibility will surface in Redwood Console as a dashboard widget that links back to source Linear issues and Confluence PRD, not as a blocker-enforcement mechanism in scheduler for MVP.
Security approval will be required for any dependency that touches customer data or private deployment config; Security asks for a 48-hour review SLAT in the workflow.
risks: Risk: Teams may under-report dependencies due to perceived project overhead. Mitigation: provide import tooling from existing project trackers and make reporting low-friction.
Risk: SLA commitments could become unrealistic during peak launches. Mitigation: include a temporary 'launch freeze' override with transparent audit logs and stakeholder approval.
Risk: Console dashboard may show stale state if sync fails. Mitigation: add failure alerts and fallback to Linear links; ensure retry/backoff for webhooks.
